core.big_idea: God provided food and water for His people in need.

passages.reading_note: Read selected verses showing the complaint, God's promise, the manna, and the daily collection.
Read selected verses showing the lack of water and God's provision from the rock.
Use only with older children to recall that the wilderness taught dependence on God.

core.metanarrative_position: Wilderness provision: after rescuing Israel from Egypt, God sustained His people as they travelled toward the promised land.

claims.statement: The Israelites complained when they lacked food in the wilderness.
God promised bread from heaven and provided manna for the people to gather each day.
When the people lacked water, God provided water from the rock.
These stories show God's patient provision for a rescued people who still needed to learn trust.

core.interpretation_skill: Retell need, complaint, God's instruction, provision, and response without turning the story into a promise of identical miracles.

learning.foundation_objective: Retell that the people needed food and water and that God provided manna and water in the wilderness.
learning.extension_objective: Explain that God's provision came after rescue and invited daily trust, while avoiding the claim that every need is met by the same kind of miracle.
know: The Israelites were travelling through the wilderness.
understand: God cared for the people even when they complained.
Daily provision taught the people to depend on God.
practise: Thank God before one meal or drink.
Share one ordinary resource with someone else.
become: A child who notices provision, expresses gratitude, and shares without shaming people who have less.
success_evidence: The child places Need, Ask, Provision, and Thank in order.
The child identifies manna and water as God's provision.
The child names one gratitude or sharing action.

zero_prep_card.objective: Children retell how God provided food and water for His people in the wilderness.
zero_prep_card.opening: Ask: What do people need every day to live and grow?
say: God had rescued His people from Egypt, but the wilderness was difficult.
The people needed food, and God provided manna for them to gather.
The people needed water, and God provided water from the rock.
God's provision invited the people to trust Him one day at a time.
ask: How can we respond to ordinary provision today?
zero_prep_card.do: Use the Need and Provision Path to place Need, Complaint, Provision, and Gratitude in order.
zero_prep_card.close: Pray: God, thank You for daily food, water, care, and people who help us.
materials: Need and Provision Path or four blank cards

preparation.passage_context: Exodus 16-17 follows the rescue through the sea. Israel has been freed but must learn to live as a dependent covenant people in a harsh environment. The narrative combines real need, grumbling, divine instruction, and patient provision.
text_observations: The people remember Egypt selectively and complain to Moses and Aaron.
God announces bread from heaven before the people know what manna is.
The collection is daily and ordered; hoarding is not the lesson goal for younger children, but dependence is visible.
Exodus 17 again places real need beside quarrelling and divine provision.
interpretation_notes: Keep the main sequence concrete: need, complaint, instruction, provision, response.
Do not describe all complaint or sadness as rebellion; the text records both real need and harmful accusation.
Do not claim that believers will never experience hunger, thirst, poverty, or delayed help.
theological_guardrails: Do not promise a miracle identical to manna or water from the rock for every present need.
Do not shame children whose households experience food insecurity or dependence on community support.
Do not teach that receiving practical help means a person has failed to trust God.

likely_questions.question: Why did the people complain if God had rescued them?
likely_questions.purpose: Explain that rescue did not instantly remove fear or teach mature trust; the wilderness exposed what they still needed to learn.

likely_questions.question: Why are some people hungry today?
likely_questions.purpose: Say the passage does not answer every cause of hunger. Christians should pray, share, serve, and seek wise adult help rather than blaming hungry people.

discussion_questions.question: What two needs appear in these passages?
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Identify where each need appears and how the people respond.

discussion_questions.question: What was manna, according to the story?
discussion_questions.foundation_prompt: Food God provided for the people to gather.
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Notice that the people first asked what it was.

discussion_questions.question: What does daily gathering teach about trust?
discussion_questions.foundation_prompt: The people depended on God each day.
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Distinguish dependence from passivity or refusing practical help.

discussion_questions.question: What is one safe way to respond to provision?
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Name gratitude, wise care, work, generosity, and receiving help without shame.

activities.title: Need and Provision Path
steps: Add Complaint and describe the people's words without acting them out loudly.
Add Gratitude and Sharing as a present response.
activities.learning_link: Makes the narrative sequence visible and separates the ancient event from modern application.
activities.low_resource_alternative: Draw four boxes on a board and point while retelling.

activities.title: Daily Provision Inventory
steps: List or draw ordinary things people need.
Circle things received through family, community, work, or creation.
Choose one safe, realistic sharing action.
activities.learning_link: Connects provision to gratitude and generosity without promising identical miracles.

closing.prayer_prompt: Thank God for daily provision and ask for generous, wise care for people in need.
closing.take_home_line: God provided food and water for His people in need.

family.title: Food and Water in the Wilderness
family.parent_intro: This study follows the concrete story of need and provision while avoiding promises that every need is met in the same way.

flow.instructions: Use the opening prompt to connect the lesson to ordinary family life.
Read Exodus 16:4, 13-18 and Exodus 17:5-6, or retell the sequence for a younger child.
Ask what the people needed, what God provided, and what daily gathering taught.
Use four household objects for Need, Complaint, Provision, and Thankfulness, then retell the story.
Choose the weekly action, then pray together.

questions: What did God provide in each passage?
What is one ordinary provision we can thank God for?

interactive.title: Need to Gratitude
interactive.instructions: Place four objects in order and say one sentence for each part of the story.

family.weekly_action: Thank someone for one practical act of provision, or choose one safe item to share this week.
family.prayer: God, thank You for food, water, care, and people who help. Make us grateful and generous.
family.parent_note: Avoid asking whether the family has enough food. If a need is disclosed, respond privately through appropriate adult support rather than turning it into a group lesson.

quiz.question: What food did God provide in the wilderness?
quiz.explanation: Exodus 16 describes manna provided for Israel.

quiz.question: What did the people need in Exodus 17?
quiz.explanation: The camp had no water to drink.

quiz.question: God provided for the people even while they were still learning to trust.
quiz.explanation: The narrative shows patient provision amid complaint.

quiz.question: Which response fits the lesson?
options: Promising every need will be met by manna
quiz.explanation: The application is gratitude and practical care, not overstatement.

puzzle.title: Need, Instruction, Provision
puzzle.instructions: Put the four parts in order.

printables.title: Need and Provision Path
printables.purpose: Help children sequence the wilderness needs and God's provision.

accessibility.reading_level: Short concrete sentences suitable for teacher-led reading with ages 4-8.
accessibility.plain_language_rule: Use concrete verbs and define every abstract term through the story.
neurodiversity_supports: Allow pointing, drawing, or one-word responses.
Give one direction at a time.
sensory_notes: Participation must not require loud noise, touch, or public performance.
non_reader_support: Use pictures, objects, or gesture-supported retelling.

do_not_ask: Do not ask children whether there is enough food at home.
Do not ask children to identify poor families in the group.
Do not imply that need proves weak faith.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Keep discussion general. If a child independently discloses unmet basic needs, follow the congregations safeguarding and practical-support process privately.
